doc.title: Marshall Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 19, 2021

title: Music as language and playing from the spirit
summary: Allen explains Sun Ra's notation needed interpretation, a thousand ways to play a note, and playing from spirit rather than from what you know.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Very interesting. Did Sun Ra include things in his written music other than actual notes? Like —

Yeah because you had to interpret it, you had to interpret what the music is. The music is a language. It’s just like a language that you study. You have to know the language and all of the syllables and the nouns and pronouns, whatever. You see? And his music was that way. It was — he told me that there was a thousand ways to play a note, band the sound, there’s a thousand ways to do it. So he had one of those ways — the way you attacked a note, and play it forward and back, instead of straight on, on, on. It’s flowing like this. See there’s forward, back. Forward, and it soothes the whole spirit and soul because it’s — that swing.

I’m so pleased you described it that way because I was envisioning if some of the musicians who were schooled like in the very precise big bands like Benny Goodman or — if they were to come in and play Sun Ra’s music he probably wouldn’t like it very precise.

Well they knew when Sun Ra would teach them how to play and what to play and to play from the spirit, not from the head, you see? It’s a difference. What you know and what you feel is two different — so he didn’t want what you knew. Cancel that, which is what? And then you want to let the spirit, right, he lived life with the spirit of things telling you more than what you know.
